extracted.intended_audience: general readers, writers, students, and scholars interested in literary forms and the novella genre
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and descriptive criteria for what constitutes a novella: its typical length, formal and thematic characteristics, structural features, and distinctions from short stories, novelettes, and novels. Useful for writers deciding form and for readers/critics classifying works.

rubrics_metrics.name: Length / word count
rubrics_metrics.description: A novella is a work of fiction intermediate in length and complexity between a short story and a novel; disagreement exists about exact page/word cutoffs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Several organizations' numeric ranges are cited: Science Fiction and Fantasy Writers Association (SFWA) / Nebula: 17,500–40,000 words (Hugo similar: 17,500–40,000); other award ranges vary (examples in article include 15,000–40,000, 17,000–35,000, 20,000–40,000). Some sources give broader ranges (e.g., ~20,000–50,000 words). At ~250 words/page this equates to roughly 70–160 pages. Related categories: novelette commonly 7,500–17,500 words (or 7,000–20,000 per The Writer); short story below those thresholds; novel often above ~50,000. The article emphasizes there is no mathematical exactness and different awards/publishers use different cutoffs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Number and complexity of conflicts
rubrics_metrics.description: Novellas generally feature fewer conflicts than a novel, yet more complex conflicts than a short story.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Conflicts in a novella have more time to develop than in short stories, allowing more depth without the sprawling multi-conflict structure of a novel. A strong novella tends to focus tightly on a limited number of conflicts to preserve unity of impression.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unity of impression / single-sitting effect
rubrics_metrics.description: Novellas may be intended to be read at a single sitting, producing a unitary effect on the reader.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because of their intermediate length, novellas often retain something of the short story's unity of impression while allowing more development. Writers can aim for an intense, concentrated exploration of theme that feels cohesive across the work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Characterization and descriptive richness
rubrics_metrics.description: Novellas contain more highly developed characterization and more luxuriant description than short stories and are often concerned with personal and emotional development.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The novella commonly emphasizes individual character development and emotional depth rather than extensive social panorama. This makes it suitable for intimate, character-driven narratives that require more space than a short story but not the novel's breadth.

rubrics_metrics.name: Formal experimentation, subplots, and point(s) of view
rubrics_metrics.description: The novella is generally not as formally experimental as the long story and the novel, and it usually lacks the subplots and multiple points of view common in novels.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: While experimentation is possible, typical novellas avoid elaborate structural demands of full-length books. Expect simpler narrative architectures: limited subplots, fewer POV shifts, and a more narrowly focused structure that supports unity and depth.

rubrics_metrics.name: Structure: chapters, sections, and use of white space
rubrics_metrics.description: Novellas may or may not be divided into chapters; white space is often used to divide sections.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Some novellas use chapter divisions (e.g., Animal Farm, The War of the Worlds), while others rely on visible breaks/white space to create sections—an option less common in short stories. Authors should choose sectioning that preserves pacing and the intended unitary effect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Narrative focus and thematic scope
rubrics_metrics.description: Novellas are most often concerned with personal and emotional development rather than with the larger social sphere.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Thematic scope tends to be narrower than a novel's; the form favors concentrated exploration of a theme or emotional arc. Writers should consider depth over breadth—intense treatment of a subject that benefits from extended focus but not broad social canvassing.

rubrics_metrics.name: German Novelle-specific formal features (Wendepunkt and symbol)
rubrics_metrics.description: In the German tradition (Novelle), the narrative is restricted to a single, suspenseful event, situation, or conflict leading to an unexpected turning point (Wendepunkt), and tends to contain a concrete symbol as the narrative's focal point.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If aiming for or evaluating a Novelle in this tradition, check for a tight causal structure culminating in a startling but logically motivated turning point, and for a concrete symbol that centers the narrative.

rubrics_metrics.name: Genre labeling and boundary subjectivity
rubrics_metrics.description: The difference between novella and novel (and novelette) is often subjective; size alone can be misleading as a classification criterion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Historical and market practices affect labeling (some works of similar length are called novels or novellas). Examples: On Chesil Beach was called a novella by its author but treated as a short novel by prize judges. Critics warn against rigid demarcation based solely on word count; consider form, structure, and effect as well as length.

rubrics_metrics.name: Practical/commercial considerations for publication
rubrics_metrics.description: Novellas face commercial challenges because they may not fit typical length requirements of magazine or book publishers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Stephen King and others note difficulty selling novellas—too long for many magazines, too short for a standalone book in some markets. Writers and editors should consider publication venue, market expectations, and possible formats (e.g., anthology, standalone small press, digital/ebook) when producing novellas.

rubrics_metrics.name: Award-specific category thresholds
rubrics_metrics.description: Literary awards often define 'novella' and 'novelette' categories by explicit word-count thresholds.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The article lists examples: Nebula/Hugo Best Novella: 17,500–40,000 (approx); Nebula/Hugo Best Novelette: ~7,500–17,500. Other awards have slightly different minima/maxima (e.g., British Fantasy Award 15,000–40,000; Paris Literary Prize 17,000–35,000; Novella Award 20,000–40,000). When submitting to awards, follow the specific organization's thresholds rather than generic definitions.
